claims.claim: Tropical Storm Irene in August 2011 cut Schmidt stability within hours in nine north-eastern lakes
claims.location: PDF p. 1 (p. A), Abstract; PDF p. 5, Results
claims.quote: Thermal stability declined within hours in all systems
claims.conditions: nine lakes AND reservoirs across 312,000 km² of north-eastern North America (GLEON buoys, 10-min to 6-h data); all stratified before the storm; stability as daily Schmidt stability

claims.claim: all but one recovered to at least 80 % of pre-storm stability within a week
claims.quote: All but one system (Ashokan) recovered to within 80% of prestorm stability within one week

claims.claim: the terrestrial inflow turned them net-heterotrophic for longer
claims.source_value: metabolism was estimated for only seven of the nine lakes; respiration rose in some (Ashokan, Rondout, Sunapee) and fell in others (Lillinonah); 'in many of our study lakes' increased carbon loading 'likely' raised R, which 'created or magnified net heterotrophic conditions'; GPP and R, coupled before the storm, were decoupled in the 10 days after; the abstract: thermal disturbance was 'shorter-lived than disturbance from inflows of terrestrial materials'

claims.note: write 'and in many of them storm-borne carbon raised respiration, creating or deepening net heterotrophy, an effect that outlasted the thermal disturbance'

claims.claim: up to 86 % of annual DOC export from forested catchments occurs in storms and snowmelt (Raymond & Saiers 2010, as cited by Klug et al. 2012)
claims.quote: up to 86% of annual DOC export from forested catchments
claims.conditions: '… has been shown to occur during these events' — the preceding sentences name storm events and snowmelt; 'including sites from the Rondout and Ashokan catchments'; ref. 24 = Raymond, P. A. & Saiers, J. E. 2010. Event controlled DOC export from forested watersheds. Biogeochemistry 100(1–3): 197–209
claims.note: the relay is accurate; the figure belongs to Raymond & Saiers, so cite them once read

notes: One correction (the net-heterotrophy sentence overgeneralizes). Other useful values: the size of the stability drop was predicted by potential volume replacement (water falling on lake + catchment ÷ lake volume): lakes split into low (≤ 26 %) and high (≥ 75 %) PVR; short-term retention time fell 50 % in Lacawac and 33 % in Croche; the change in GPP tracked the change in temperature (r² = 0.67); recovery of stability was related to the size of the initial effect (r² = 0.5).
